title: Running average with a unit-width box
notes: The irregular illustrative signal is a finite trigonometric sum. Each Fourier mode is integrated exactly over the unit-width box, so the dashed curve is its actual convolution and the marked value is the corresponding integral. The box has mass one.

title: Shannon scaling: reference scale
notes: The chapter scaling convention is phi_(j,n)(x)=2^(-j/2) phi(2^(-j)x-n). The actual Shannon scaling function sinc is used, with common horizontal coordinate x/2^j and amplitude measured relative to 2^(-j/2). The three centers are 0, 4 times 2^j, and 0; their relative scales are 1, 2, and 1/2 and peaks 1, 1/sqrt(2), and sqrt(2). The original third image was translated despite its n=0 caption.

title: Ordered coefficients and an admissible threshold
notes: The plotted values are the nonincreasing discrete sequence d_m=3.2 m^(-0.65), with M=5. T lies between d_6 and d_5, so strict thresholding retains exactly five coefficients. The source diagram incorrectly put T at the retained value d_M. The tail-energy formula uses orthonormality.

title: Hard thresholding with precise endpoints
notes: The chapter retains coefficients only when their magnitude is strictly greater than T. The diagonal branches therefore have open endpoints at +/-T, while the zero branch has closed endpoints there. Vertical jump segments are omitted because they are not part of the function graph.

title: Hard thresholding and integer quantization
notes: The horizontal coordinate is x/T; the hard-threshold output is divided by T so both vertical axes are dimensionless. Hard thresholding sends +/-T to zero, whereas the chapter integer quantizer sends them to +/-1. All open and closed endpoints follow these definitions. In particular the quantizer zero bin is open at both ends.

title: Uniform probability distribution
notes: All three illustrations use the same seven-symbol alphabet (-3,...,3) and a common vertical scale. The probabilities are p_i=1/7 for every symbol. They are nonnegative and sum to one. Entropy is log_2(7), approximately 2.807 bits, using the convention 0 log(0)=0. These exact illustrative distributions clarify the original schematic examples; they are not empirical measurements recovered from the old image.

title: Point mass probability distribution
notes: All three illustrations use the same seven-symbol alphabet (-3,...,3) and a common vertical scale. The probabilities are p_0=1 and p_i=0 otherwise. They are nonnegative and sum to one. Entropy is zero bits, using the convention 0 log(0)=0. These exact illustrative distributions clarify the original schematic examples; they are not empirical measurements recovered from the old image.

title: Concentrated probability distribution
notes: All three illustrations use the same seven-symbol alphabet (-3,...,3) and a common vertical scale. The probabilities are (0.04, 0.10, 0.20, 0.32, 0.20, 0.10, 0.04). They are nonnegative and sum to one. Entropy is approximately 2.491 bits, using the convention 0 log(0)=0. These exact illustrative distributions clarify the original schematic examples; they are not empirical measurements recovered from the old image.

title: Hard and soft thresholding
notes: Solid hard thresholding has open diagonal endpoints and closed zero endpoints at +/-T. Dashed soft thresholding is continuous and subtracts T from the retained magnitude. No vertical line is drawn across a discontinuity; both functions are zero exactly at the cutoffs.

title: Smoothed absolute value, epsilon=0.1
notes: Exact graphs of |x| and sqrt(x^2+epsilon^2), with epsilon=0.1. Both panels use identical axes near the origin, making the smoothing scale comparable. The smoothed function lies above absolute value and has value epsilon and derivative zero at the origin. The old plots were too coarse to reliably convey the stated epsilon values.
